To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed framework MMGreen, which is a joint computing plus communications optimization framework, may significantly reduce the total energy cost with respect to the state-of-art resource provisioning strategies, by dynamically adapting the number of active nodes to the actual workload and by using the DVFS technology to dynamically adjust the CPU frequencies.

(i) the proposed framework can significantly improve energy efficiency of cloud systems by jointly optimizing the computing resources and the network bandwidth; (ii) MMGreen is able to adapt the system to the actual workload, by dynamically adjusting the amount of resources to be used, and (iii) MMGreen can reduce the overall energy cost by up to 40% with respect to a state-of-the-art approach, while respecting SLA requirements.

MMGreen, the proposed joint computing plus communication energy optimization framework for big data multimedia processing, can achieve significant energy savings with respect to the state of the art approaches.

a novel approach to the design and implementation of a cloud system, that is capable to dynamically adapt the resources allocation to the actual workload.
the design of an energy efficient and cost effective multimedia processing in cloud systems.

a new approach to energy-efficient multimedia processing on cloud systems, which can be applied to other types of services as well, and it is a first step towards the realization of a green cloud computing.
